# Hybrid and Diffusion Representations

Also called: Feed-forward Gaussian Generation, Gaussian Diffusion, TriplaneGaussian

## Overview
This family addresses the problem of generating a complete set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$ from a single input (image or text) without per-scene optimization, which is required by methods like [Adaptive Density Control](9188-adaptive-density-control.md). It sets itself apart by using feed-forward neural networks or [diffusion models](#10443-diffusion-models-ddpms.md) to predict Gaussian parameters directly, rather than optimizing them via gradient descent on a fixed or dynamically densified set.

## Shared principles
The methods in this family share the goal of mapping a compact input representation to an explicit 3D Gaussian field $\mathcal{G} = \{ \mu_i, \Sigma_i, \alpha_i, c_i \}_{i=1}^{N}$. Unlike [Adaptive Density Control](9188-adaptive-density-control.md), which iteratively modifies $\mathcal{G}$ based on rendering gradients, these methods produce $\mathcal{G}$ in a single forward pass (or sampling step). The core challenge is ensuring geometric consistency across viewpoints and avoiding artifacts like "floaters" (spurious Gaussians) or the "Janus problem" (inconsistent geometry from different angles) [S1].

## Subtopics

### [TriplaneGaussian](7558-triplanegaussian.md)
[TriplaneGaussian](#7558-triplanegaussian.md) is a feed-forward method that combines a sparse point cloud with a dense tri-plane feature encoding. It solves the problem of single-image 3D reconstruction by first generating a coarse point cloud and tri-plane features from image embeddings, then querying the tri-planes at point locations to predict Gaussian attributes. It differs from [GaussianDiffusion](9190-gaussiandiffusion.md) by using explicit feature querying rather than a voxel-based diffusion process. See [TriplaneGaussian](7558-triplanegaussian.md) for implementation details.

### [GaussianDiffusion](9190-gaussiandiffusion.md)
[GaussianDiffusion](#9190-gaussiandiffusion.md) trains a 3D diffusion model on a **GaussianCube** representation to generate 3D Gaussian fields directly from compact inputs. It solves the generation consistency problem by mapping a structured latent space (voxel grid) to explicit Gaussian parameters via optimal transport. It differs from [TriplaneGaussian](7558-triplanegaussian.md) by using a [voxel-based representation](#10852-voxel-based-representation.md) and diffusion sampling rather than tri-plane feature querying. See [GaussianDiffusion](9190-gaussiandiffusion.md) for implementation details.

### Text2Immersion
#### definition
A scene generation method similar to LucidDreamer but with outlier removal and two-stage optimization [S1].
#### step
A process removes outliers in the point cloud [S1]. 3DGS optimization has two stages: training coarse 3DGS and refinement [S1].

## Background
The need for hybrid and diffusion representations arises from the high computational cost of per-scene optimization in standard 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md). Early works like LucidDreamer used diffusion priors to guide 3DGS optimization [S1]. Recent advances have moved towards fully feed-forward architectures (e.g., TriplaneGaussian) or generative diffusion models operating directly on Gaussian parameters (e.g., GaussianDiffusion) to enable instant 3D scene synthesis from text or single images [S1].
